topStories.headline: The Mess Hall Opens at Presidio Tunnel Tops, Bringing All-Day Dining to the National Park
topStories.dek: A long-anticipated 6,200-square-foot food hall opens this Saturday at Presidio Tunnel Tops, giving the national park its most ambitious dining destination yet.
topStories.body:
After years of planning and permitting delays inside a historic 1897 former U.S. Army building, The Mess Hall at the Presidio officially opens to the public on Saturday, August 15, 2026, at 201 Halleck Street within the Presidio Tunnel Tops. The food hall spans a 6,200-square-foot indoor-outdoor space with sweeping views of the San Francisco Bay, Alcatraz Island, and the Golden Gate Bridge.

The venue is designed as an all-day dining destination, open Monday through Thursday from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. and Friday through Sunday from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. It houses three distinct restaurant concepts under one roof: Dayboat Seafood, offering oysters, scallops, and seafood classics; Boda, featuring Korean dishes including fried chicken, banchan, and mandu; and Breadwinner, serving smashburgers, hoagies, and vegetarian sandwiches. The venue also includes a café serving Wrecking Ball Coffee, a full cocktail-wine-beer bar, and a specialty retail market.

James Beard Award-winning chef and author Peter Serpico led the development of the food concepts and culinary offerings. The bar program is curated by Zach Negin, known for his work with Tabula Rasa Bar and other San Francisco establishments.

The Mess Hall's arrival marks a significant shift for the Presidio's food scene, which has been building momentum with other recent openings including Maria Isabel, a Mexican restaurant at 500 Presidio Avenue that earned a Michelin Exceptional Cocktails Award for 2026. Together, these additions are reshaping the park's northern edge into what observers are calling a genuine neighborhood dining destination.

topStories.headline: Presidio Trust Gets New Board as Benioff Named Chair, Traina Vice Chair
topStories.dek: Three months after Trump fired all six Biden-appointed trustees, the reconstituted Presidio Trust Board of Directors has elected its leadership and begun operating.
topStories.body:
The Presidio Trust Board of Directors has elected Lynne Benioff as Board Chair and Trevor Traina as Vice Chair, according to a July 27, 2026 announcement from the Trust. The board was formed after President Donald Trump fired all six Biden-appointed members in April and replaced them with new appointees in May.

The six new members, appointed by the White House on May 14, 2026, are: Lynne Benioff, co-chair of Time magazine and a former Presidio Trust board chair from 2015 to 2025; Trevor Traina, a technology entrepreneur and diplomat who serves as Chief Business Officer at Tools for Humanity; John Bickford, managing partner at Local Capital Group and Governance Committee Chair; Stanford Graduate School of Business educator Laura Arrillaga-Andreessen; James Burnham, general counsel at xAI and X and DOGE attorney; and Kyle Corcoran, CFO of Redpanda and a Marine veteran who holds the seat reserved for veterans.

The firings of the previous board in April had sparked significant concern from community members and local officials. Trump first targeted the Presidio Trust in a February 2025 executive order that labeled the agency an "unnecessary governmental entity." San Francisco Supervisor Stephen Sherrill, whose District 2 includes the Presidio, described the climate as "unprecedented" at the time.

The Presidio Trust is a unique federal corporation that earns its own revenue to maintain and operate the 1,500-acre national park site without ongoing federal appropriations. The park hosts approximately 9.5 million visits per year. CEO Jean Fraser, who had announced plans to step down, continued in her role through the leadership transition.

topStories.headline: Rose Pizzeria's SF Debut on Clement Street Has Been Booked Solid Since Day One
topStories.dek: The Berkeley pizzeria named among America's best by the New York Times opened its first San Francisco outpost at 1 Clement Street this spring, instantly reshaping the Inner Richmond's dining landscape.
topStories.body:
Rose Pizzeria, the Berkeley-born restaurant that the New York Times named one of the 22 best pizzerias in the United States in 2024, has opened its first San Francisco location at 1 Clement Street in the Inner Richmond — and it arrived to a frenzy. Before the restaurant served its first pizza to the general public, there was not a single table available to reserve within the following month.

Owners Gerad Gobel and Alexis Rorabaugh, a married couple who previously operated an Italian restaurant in Chicago, took over the former Village Pizzeria space at Clement and Arguello. The new location is considerably larger than the Berkeley flagship, allowing for customizable pies for the first time, with diners able to add toppings such as mushrooms, sausage, pepperoni, or pickled chiles. The menu still features the signature topping combinations that made Rose famous, including the She Wolf pie with burrata, slow-roasted tomato, garlic confit, olives, capers, and Sicilian oregano.

The San Francisco Standard reviewed the restaurant in June, noting its unafraid approach to polarizing ingredients — the Beach Club pie topped with pistachio mortadella, pickled jalapeño, and pineapple has been particularly talked-about. The restaurant is open Monday through Sunday, 11:30 a.m. to 9 p.m., and takes reservations online, though walk-ins are welcome at the counter and outside tables during non-peak hours.

events.title: EXCLUSION: The Presidio's Role in WWII Japanese American Incarceration
events.location: Presidio Officers' Club, 50 Moraga Avenue, Presidio
events.description: The award-winning free exhibition examines the Presidio's role as the Army's Western Defense Command in the unjust incarceration of 120,000 Japanese Americans during World War II. Open Fridays through Sundays, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., through August 31.

events.title: Presidio Habitat Stewards — Weekly Volunteer Days
events.location: Presidio of San Francisco (location provided at registration)
events.description: Volunteers of all ages help restore natural areas and create wildlife corridors in the Presidio every Saturday and on the first and third Wednesdays of each month from 9 a.m. to noon. No experience necessary; tools and training provided. Registration required.

events.title: Heart of the Richmond District Night Market — Final Summer Edition
events.location: Clement Street between 22nd and 25th Avenue, Outer Richmond
events.description: The final edition of this summer's free neighborhood night market fills several blocks of Clement Street with local food vendors, two live performance stages, DJs, arts and crafts, and community organizations. New in 2026: expanded hot food offerings and additional entertainment zones. Free and open to the public, 4–8 p.m.
events.sourceName: Heart of the Richmond District Night Market

events.title: The Mess Hall Grand Opening at Presidio Tunnel Tops
events.location: The Mess Hall, 201 Halleck St., Presidio Tunnel Tops
events.description: The highly anticipated food hall opens its doors with three restaurant concepts — Dayboat Seafood, Boda (Korean), and Breadwinner (burgers and sandwiches) — plus a Wrecking Ball Coffee café, full cocktail bar, and specialty market, all inside a restored 1897 Army building with Bay views.

events.title: Presidio Habitat Stewards — Saturday Morning
events.description: Join the recurring Saturday volunteer habitat restoration program at the Presidio — plant, weed, water, and mulch alongside park staff. Registration required through the Golden Gate National Parks Conservancy website.

events.title: Presidio Native Plant Nursery Work Day
events.description: Help care for more than 100,000 native plants used in Presidio restoration sites; this drop-in volunteer session runs from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. at the Presidio Native Plant Nursery.

events.title: 250 Years on the Presidio — NPS Ranger-Led Walk
events.location: Presidio Visitor Center, 210 Lincoln Blvd near Anza, Presidio
events.description: Walk the Tunnel Tops and the historic Main Post of the Presidio with a National Park Service guide, exploring layers of history from the Ohlone people through the Army era and into the park's future, as part of the 250th anniversary commemoration year.

events.title: Los Californianos: Anza 250/America 250 Living History Ceremony
events.location: Presidio Officers' Club & Main Post, Presidio
events.description: A living history program marking the 250th anniversary of El Presidio de San Francisco's founding, featuring an entry procession, flag ceremonies, historical reenactors, musical performances by Los Arribeños de San Francisco and the Young American Patriots Fife & Drum Corps, and a roll call of the 240 men, women, and children of the Anza Expedition.

moreNews.headline: Presidio Marks 250th Anniversary with Year-Long Programming
moreNews.body: The Presidio of San Francisco is commemorating its 250th anniversary this year — the founding of El Presidio de San Francisco took place on September 17, 1776, at the very same time the Declaration of Independence was being signed on the East Coast. Throughout 2026, the Presidio Trust and its partners have offered special programs, exhibitions, and events honoring the park's layered history spanning Ramaytush Ohlone stewardship, Spanish and Mexican eras, and U.S. military use. The anniversary culminates with a living history ceremony on September 17 at the Presidio Officers' Club.

moreNews.headline: Richmond Review Editor Michael Durand Dies, Leaving Legacy of Neighborhood Journalism
moreNews.body: Newspaper editor Michael Durand, who owned and edited two Richmond District neighborhood papers — the Richmond Review and the Sunset Beacon — died recently, according to Mission Local. Durand was recognized as a champion of hyperlocal journalism in the Richmond and Sunset districts. The papers he helmed continue to publish community news, announcements, and neighborhood coverage.

moreNews.headline: SF 55+ Neighborhood Walks Include Weekly Richmond Routes
moreNews.body: San Francisco's free 55+ Neighborhood Walks program runs weekly routes accessible to seniors of varying abilities, including a Tuesday walk departing at noon from Angelina's Cafe at 6000 California St. (at 22nd Avenue) in the Richmond District, heading to Lands End and back. Walks are free, meet-up-based, and require no advance registration — participants can also simply show up in person. Check meetup.com/sf-55-neighborhood-walking-groups for the latest schedule and weather cancellations.

moreNews.headline: Balboa Theatre Celebrated Its Centennial This Spring Under Nonprofit Stewardship
moreNews.body: The Balboa Theatre in the Outer Richmond marked its 100th year in April 2026 with free community screenings, a fundraising gala, and the unveiling of a new tile mural titled "A Century of Filmmaking in San Francisco" by artists Sandow Birk and Elyse Pignolet. CinemaSFbay, the nonprofit now operating the theater, stretched the centennial celebration into a weeklong series of screenings. The Balboa, which first opened on February 27, 1926, continues to operate at 3630 Balboa Street, screening independent films, foreign cinema, and cult classics.

restaurants.name: Rose Pizzeria
restaurants.description: Berkeley-born pizzeria named among America's best by the New York Times, now open at the corner of Clement and Arguello with customizable thin-crust pies and natural wine.

restaurants.name: Burma Superstar
restaurants.description: The original Clement Street location of this beloved Burmese institution, famous since 1992 for its tea leaf salad, samusa soup, and rainbow salad.

restaurants.name: B Star
restaurants.description: Sister restaurant to Burma Superstar on Clement Street serving healthy Asian-inspired comfort food with influences from Thailand, China, Burma, India, Japan, and California.

restaurants.name: Wako Japanese Restaurant
restaurants.description: Intimate Michelin-starred sushi counter on Clement Street offering omakase and sushi tasting experiences with seasonally driven Japanese ingredients.

restaurants.name: Chapeau!
restaurants.description: Classic French bistro beloved in the Inner Richmond since 1996, offering both à la carte and prix-fixe menus in a warm, intimate setting.

restaurants.name: Arsicault Bakery
restaurants.description: Celebrated Inner Richmond bakery named best new bakery in the U.S. by Bon Appétit, renowned for its flaky, buttery croissants with lines that routinely snake down Arguello Boulevard.

restaurants.name: Giorgio's Pizzeria
restaurants.description: Family-owned Italian restaurant serving pizza, pasta, and Italian classics in the Inner Richmond for over 40 years.

restaurants.name: Heritage Restaurant & Bar
restaurants.description: Clement Street restaurant offering fresh seasonal California cuisine in a comfortable setting with a full bar, private dining space, and a fireplace.

restaurants.name: Breadbelly
restaurants.description: Inner Richmond bakery from alums of Atelier Crenn serving Filipino-inspired pastries, Malaysian kaya toast, and rotating savory sandwiches.

restaurants.name: Maria Isabel
restaurants.description: From the team behind Dalida, this Presidio Avenue Mexican restaurant draws on Acapulco coastal flavors with heirloom corn, California seafood, and seasonal produce, earning a 2026 Michelin Exceptional Cocktails Award.

restaurants.name: Mess Hall at the Presidio
restaurants.description: Newly opened 6,200-square-foot all-day food hall at Presidio Tunnel Tops featuring Dayboat Seafood, Boda (Korean), and Breadwinner (burgers), plus a Wrecking Ball Coffee café, cocktail bar, and specialty market, led by James Beard Award-winning chef Peter Serpico.

restaurants.name: Marla Bakery
restaurants.description: Beloved Outer Richmond bakery started by two former Nopa chefs, now one of the city's top brunch destinations.

restaurants.name: Pacific Cafe
restaurants.description: Outer Richmond seafood institution since the early 1970s, famous for fresh-caught fish, chalkboard daily specials, and complimentary white wine offered while guests wait for a table.

restaurants.name: Simple Pleasures Cafe
restaurants.description: Beloved Outer Richmond café owned since 1994 by Ahmed Riad and Diana Riggio, known for its vibrant community atmosphere and sunny sidewalk seating on Balboa Street.

restaurants.name: House of Bagels
restaurants.description: Outer Richmond institution serving Brooklyn-style bagels and classic Jewish deli fare since 1962.

restaurants.name: Lokma
restaurants.description: Outer Richmond Turkish and Mediterranean restaurant at 19th Avenue offering outdoor dining, weekend brunch, and dinner nightly.

restaurants.name: Moscow & Tbilisi Bakery
restaurants.description: Outer Richmond 'Little Russia' staple offering affordable potato piroshki, blintzes, and Eastern European baked goods to go.

restaurants.name: Violet's
restaurants.description: Outer Richmond sister restaurant to Fiorella, serving elevated American bar food including seafood platters, clam toast, and shrimp louie rolls from chef Dante Cecchini paired with creative cocktails.

restaurants.name: Kissaten Hifi
restaurants.description: Richmond café blending Japanese and Filipino cafe culture with great matcha, espresso drinks, and lots of vinyl records.

restaurants.name: Dumpling King
restaurants.description: Popular Richmond District Chinese restaurant praised for its excellent hand-made dumplings and broad menu of Northern Chinese dishes.

hotels.name: Inn at the Presidio
hotels.description: A TripAdvisor Travelers' Choice Best of the Best winner housed in a restored historic Army barracks at the Presidio, offering European-style breakfast buffets and complimentary afternoon wine and cheese by the firepit.

hotels.name: Lodge at the Presidio
hotels.description: Sister property to the Inn at the Presidio, also set within the national park in a beautifully restored historic building, offering pet-friendly and family-friendly stays with Bay and Golden Gate views.

shops.name: Green Apple Books
shops.description: San Francisco Legacy Business founded in 1967 and named Publishers Weekly's best bookstore of 2014, carrying an enormous selection of new and used books, records, and gifts at Clement and Sixth Avenue.

shops.name: Park Life
shops.type: Art gallery and design retail store
shops.description: Voted best place to find a gift by San Francisco Magazine, this Inner Richmond hybrid gallery and retail space carries hard-to-find art books, prints, design objects, t-shirts, and homewares alongside 10 rotating gallery exhibitions per year.

artEntertainment.name: Walt Disney Family Museum
artEntertainment.description: A 40,000-square-foot non-profit museum in a restored 1897 Presidio barracks featuring 10 interactive galleries on Walt Disney's life and legacy, narrated in his own voice, with a spectacular model of the original Disneyland.

artEntertainment.name: Presidio Officers' Club
artEntertainment.description: Free cultural venue in the Presidio's oldest standing structure, hosting the award-winning EXCLUSION exhibition on Japanese American incarceration and other cultural programming through the Presidio Trust.

artEntertainment.name: Balboa Theater
artEntertainment.description: Outer Richmond landmark cinema opened in 1926, now operated by nonprofit CinemaSFbay, screening independent films, foreign cinema, cult classics, and hosting special events including stand-up comedy nights and film festivals.

artEntertainment.name: Park Life Gallery
artEntertainment.description: Inner Richmond gallery space at 220 Clement Street holding 10 exhibitions per year focused on contemporary painting, drawing, and mixed media, connected to the Park Life retail store.

gymsRecreation.name: Presidio Tunnel Tops
gymsRecreation.description: Award-winning 14-acre public park atop the Highway 101 tunnels in the Presidio, featuring meadows, nature playgrounds, campfire circles, trails, and sweeping views of the Golden Gate Bridge and San Francisco Bay.

gymsRecreation.name: Presidio Golf Course
gymsRecreation.description: One of the most historic golf courses on the West Coast, set within the Presidio national park with views of the Golden Gate Bridge; open to the public year-round.

gymsRecreation.name: Crissy Field
gymsRecreation.description: Restored tidal marsh and beach promenade along the Presidio's northern waterfront, offering the Golden Gate Promenade trail and Bay Trail for walking, running, cycling, and picnicking with Golden Gate Bridge views.

gymsRecreation.name: Mountain Lake Park
gymsRecreation.description: Lone Mountain neighborhood park anchored by a restored freshwater lake, offering walking paths, a children's playground, tennis courts, and habitat for migratory birds.

gymsRecreation.name: Baker Beach
gymsRecreation.description: A one-mile sandy beach at the southern edge of the Presidio with dramatic views directly beneath the Golden Gate Bridge, popular for walking, picnicking, and photography.

gymsRecreation.name: Richmond District YMCA
gymsRecreation.description: Full-service community YMCA in the Inner Richmond offering fitness facilities, group exercise classes, aquatics, youth programs, and community partnerships throughout the neighborhood.
